newsitem.title: UK: Higher costs dampen Henderson Q1 pre-tax.
newsitem.headline: Higher costs dampen Henderson Q1 pre-tax.

text.p: Henderson Plc said on Friday increased operating expenses had left first quarter pre-tax profits flat, but it raised assets under management by 6.7 percent in the period.
Reporting results for the three months to end-June, the independent fund manager said it raised revenues 7.5 percent from a year earlier to 20.2 million sterling.
But business development investment, increased business volumes and provision of market competitive staff incentives drove operating expenses 13.5 percent up to 16.4 million.
Pre-tax earnings were 5.2 million sterling against a comparable 5.3 million, and earnings per share 16.07 pence versus 16.31.
Funds under management rose 6.7 percent to 14 billion sterling since the start of the financial year, and net client gains were 125 million sterling, the company said.

Henderson said the acquisition of the outstanding interest in Henderson Real Estate Strategy in the quarter would provide significant growth opportunities, both for UK and European institutional markets.

Chairman Ben Wrey said Henderson's investment performance record remained competitive over the short and medium term, pointing to outperformance of UK pension fund industry averages in segregated and pooled funds.
